chains.title: GATA2 mediates the allele-sensitive LMO1 regulatory effect

links.claim: GATA2 is a leading candidate because it occupies the variant in SK-N-SH and is highly expressed there. The literature describes an allele-sensitive GATA motif: ref C corresponds to G on the complementary strand and alt A to T, changing GATA to TATA. Thus stronger ref binding is plausible, but not directly measured for GATA2; no allele-specific QBiC-SELEX result is provided, and the literature does not distinguish GATA2 from GATA3.
The variant lies in enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1518342, which has enhancer-associated chromatin marks; the reported maxima are not specific to SK-N-SH.

LMO1 is the leading candidate target because the variant is intronic to it and LMO1 has the strongest reported gene-link scores, but direct regulation of LMO1 by this cCRE is not shown. The skeletal-muscle eQTL is not neuroblastoma evidence, and no Brain-Cortex eQTL was reported.

The proposed context is adrenergic neuroblastoma: GATA2 occupancy is observed in SK-N-SH, while the literature connects the locus genotype with adrenergic versus mesenchymal tumor states; GATA2-specific mediation in that state is not established.

The ref-associated GATA motif is consistent with greater neuroblastoma susceptibility than alt: the cited zebrafish result reports reduced tumor penetrance for the protective TATA allele, which corresponds to alt A. This supports an allele-to-phenotype connection but does not establish GATA2 mediation.

predictions: In relevant cells, GATA2 occupancy should be greater on ref C than alt A.
Selective GATA2 depletion should reduce the allele-dependent LMO1 regulatory difference more than selective GATA3 depletion.
falsified_if: A suitable allele-specific assay shows no greater GATA2 binding on ref, or shows greater binding on alt.
GATA2 depletion leaves the allele-dependent LMO1 response unchanged while GATA3 depletion removes it.

chains.title: GATA3 rather than GATA2 mediates the allele-sensitive LMO1 regulatory effect

links.claim: GATA3 occupies the variant in SK-N-SH, making it a plausible mediator of the reported GATA-motif change. Ref C corresponds to G on the complementary strand and alt A to T, changing GATA to TATA; stronger ref binding is plausible but not directly measured for GATA3. No allele-specific QBiC-SELEX result is provided, and the literature does not distinguish GATA3 from GATA2.
The variant lies in enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1518342, which has enhancer-associated chromatin marks; the reported maxima are not specific to SK-N-SH.

LMO1 is the leading candidate target because the variant is intronic to it and LMO1 has the strongest reported gene-link scores, but direct regulation of LMO1 by this cCRE is not shown. The skeletal-muscle eQTL is not neuroblastoma evidence, and no Brain-Cortex eQTL was reported.

The proposed context is adrenergic neuroblastoma: GATA3 occupancy is observed in SK-N-SH, and the literature connects the locus genotype with tumor cell state, but GATA3-specific mediation in adrenergic cells is not established.

A GATA3-mediated effect would be consistent with the reported lower tumor penetrance of the protective TATA allele corresponding to alt A, but the phenotype evidence does not attribute that effect specifically to GATA3.

predictions: In relevant cells, GATA3 occupancy should be greater on ref C than alt A.
Selective GATA3 depletion should reduce the allele-dependent LMO1 regulatory difference more than selective GATA2 depletion.
falsified_if: A suitable allele-specific assay shows no greater GATA3 binding on ref, or shows greater binding on alt.
GATA3 depletion leaves the allele-dependent LMO1 response unchanged while GATA2 depletion removes it.

chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of this variant
predictions: The observed occupancy and motif annotation may not produce a variant-dependent TF effect; the association may instead reflect a linked causal change or another mechanism.
Factor-specific depletion should not reveal a reproducible allele-dependent LMO1 response attributable to GATA2 or GATA3.
falsified_if: A reproducible allele-dependent GATA2- or GATA3-mediated change in LMO1 regulation is demonstrated in relevant neuroblastoma cells.

grades_v0.reason: GATA2 ChIP-seq peaks overlap the variant in SK-N-SH, and the literature identifies a GATA motif affected by the allele change. But there is no allele-specific QBiC-SELEX result or other direct measurement showing stronger GATA2 binding to ref C. The motif evidence does not distinguish GATA2 from GATA3.

E03 directly places the variant in the enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1518342 and reports enhancer-associated chromatin marks. The claim appropriately notes that the reported maxima are not SK-N-SH-specific.
LMO1 is intronic to the variant and has the strongest reported L2G score, supporting it as a leading candidate. These data do not directly establish that this cCRE regulates LMO1.

GATA2 occupancy is shown in SK-N-SH, and the cited literature links the locus genotype to adrenergic versus mesenchymal tumor states. The evidence does not directly establish the proposed GATA2-mediated effect in adrenergic neuroblastoma cells.

The cited zebrafish result directly reports reduced tumor penetrance for the protective TATA allele. Given the stated strand mapping, that allele corresponds to alt A. The result supports the allele-to-phenotype direction, though not GATA2-specific mediation.

GATA3 ChIP-seq peaks overlap the variant in SK-N-SH, and the literature supports an allele-sensitive GATA motif. No allele-specific QBiC-SELEX result establishes the direction for GATA3 specifically. The evidence also does not justify selecting GATA3 over the more highly expressed, likewise occupied GATA2.

The protective TATA allele is linked to reduced tumor penetrance in zebrafish, but the cited evidence does not attribute that phenotype to GATA3 rather than another GATA factor or another mechanism.

checks.why: Could clarify whether the cited study measures allele-specific binding and whether it identifies GATA2, GATA3, or only a GATA-family motif.
Could add disease-association evidence for LMO1 in neuroblastoma and help distinguish gene-level support from the broader GWAS and variant-level evidence.
Could test whether the variant has a relevant neural-tissue LMO1 eQTL, complementing the reported skeletal-muscle eQTL.

args.query: PMID 37183825 rs2168101 GATA2 GATA3 allele-specific binding reporter assay

matrix.test: In SK-N-SH cells, compare allele-paired enhancer reporter activity after selective GATA2 or GATA3 depletion.

outcomes.outcome: The ref-versus-alt reporter difference is reduced more by GATA2 depletion than by GATA3 depletion.
The ref-versus-alt reporter difference is reduced more by GATA3 depletion than by GATA2 depletion.
No reproducible allele-dependent reporter difference, or no selective effect of either depletion on such a difference.

matrix.test: Measure allele-specific GATA2 and GATA3 occupancy at the endogenous site in heterozygous SK-N-SH cells.

outcomes.outcome: GATA2 occupancy favors ref C; this assay alone need not show that GATA2 is the functional mediator.
GATA3 occupancy favors ref C; this assay alone need not show that GATA3 is the functional mediator.
No reproducible allele-specific occupancy difference for the proposed mediator.

matrix.test: Perturb cCRE EH38E1518342 and measure endogenous LMO1 expression in an appropriate neuroblastoma model.

outcomes.outcome: Perturbing the element changes LMO1 expression; this alone does not identify GATA2 as the mediator.
Perturbing the element changes LMO1 expression; this alone does not identify GATA3 as the mediator.
No reproducible LMO1 response attributable to this element and variant.

next_experiment: Run the allele-paired enhancer reporter in SK-N-SH cells with selective GATA2 versus GATA3 depletion, measuring the ref-versus-alt activity difference. This is the cheapest proposed test that distinguishes the two leading TF-specific chains.

Our data suggest that LMO1 overexpression in MYCN-amplified NB cells increases the pro-metastatic properties of macrophages in the tumor-cell microenvironment, which is important for driving NB metastasis.
We found LMO1 rs2168101 G > T and rs11603024 C > T as well as LMO2 rs7933499 G > A were significantly associated with Wilms tumor risk.

Fourteen loci, including ten protective polymorphisms from CASC15, BARD1, LMO1, HSD17B12, and HACE1, and four risk variants from BARD1, RSRC1, CPZ and MMP20 were significantly associated with neuroblastoma risk.
Both LMO1 expression levels and the risk of developing neuroblastoma in children are associated with a single nucleotide polymorphism, G/T, that affects a GATA motif in the first intron of LMO1.

Here, we showed that WT zebrafish with the GATA genotype developed adrenergic neuroblastoma, while knock-in of the protective TATA allele at this locus reduced the penetrance of MYCN-driven tumors, which were restricted to the mesenchymal cell state.
They now demonstrate experimentally, using genome-edited zebrafish, that a polymorphism in the human rs2168101 locus of the LMO1 gene determines which CRC is active in a tumor.
